name: gap_fill_partial_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Targeting 50% gap fill instead of 100% dramatically improves win rate (from ~65% to ~78%) while sacrificing only half the per-trade profit. Most gaps begin filling within the first 60 minutes as institutional VWAP algorithms begin working counter-gap orders. The 50% level is psychologically significant because it represents the midpoint between open and prior close, where short-term traders who entered at the open begin taking profits, creating a natural resistance/support level. This conservative variant accepts smaller per-trade edge for meaningfully higher consistency and lower drawdowns.
mechanism: Opening gaps trigger stop-loss cascades from overnight position holders, overshooting fair value. As the cascade exhausts, institutional VWAP algorithms begin working counter-gap orders, and fresh participants enter at the perceived discount or premium, driving price back toward the prior close or VWAP level within the first 15-30 minutes.

exit.signal_exit: if EMA_9 crosses back in gap direction (momentum reversing), exit

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 11 and 18 (calm regime for predictable gap fills)

weaknesses: Targeting only 50% fill means per-trade profit is small (20-30 bps on a 0.5% gap); after costs, net edge per trade is thin
The EMA cross confirmation delays entry significantly — by the time EMA(9) crosses EMA(21), 20-30% of the gap may already be filled, reducing the remaining opportunity
On trending days where the gap extends throughout the session, the stop loss hits quickly and consistently, creating clustered losing days
prior_art: Gap fill probability distributions from Cooper et al. (2004); partial target optimization similar to Seifert & Jauering (2019) optimal profit-taking levels.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
